articles.title: Planning rest stops when public seating is unavailable
articles.summary: Offline planning and recordkeeping guidance for planning rest stops when public seating is unavailable.

visual.alt: A three-part route schematic labelled Usual stop, Alternative, Confirm. It summarises safe information gathering and planning for planning rest stops when public seating is unavailable, not actual live conditions or a hazardous procedure.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid; current instructions from the responsible organisation take precedence.

sections.title: Understand the local arrangement
paragraphs: On a familiar route, note places where public seating is normally provided, distinguishing outdoor benches from staffed premises with admission or opening restrictions. A map symbol does not establish that a seat is currently usable.

Consider whether the journey offers enough opportunities to pause for the people travelling, including anyone with reduced stamina. Record a shorter alternative rather than assuming everyone can complete the original distance.

sections.title: Prepare and verify a practical alternative
paragraphs: Where practical, confirm opening hours and accessibility with the responsible operator before leaving. If conditions change, prioritise a safe accessible alternative rather than continuing to an uncertain rest point.
Keep a paper note of possible rest locations, their limitations and the date last checked. Do not publish someone else's personal mobility needs in a shared guide.

articles.title: Agreeing a temporary parcel handover in a shared building
articles.summary: Offline planning and recordkeeping guidance for agreeing a temporary parcel handover in a shared building.

visual.alt: A three-part sequence schematic labelled Agree, Record, Confirm. It summarises safe information gathering and planning for agreeing a temporary parcel handover in a shared building, not actual live conditions or a hazardous procedure.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid; current instructions from the responsible organisation take precedence.

sections.title: Understand the local arrangement
paragraphs: When a communal entrance or parcel room is unavailable, ask the manager or carrier what temporary arrangements are authorised. A neighbour's suggestion does not automatically change delivery rules.
If another adult agrees to receive an item, record their consent and agreed method without displaying access codes, tracking links or flat numbers on a public noticeboard.

sections.title: Prepare and verify a practical alternative
paragraphs: Note the carrier, reference, recipient, agreed collection point and date in a private household record. Avoid unnecessary descriptions of parcel contents.
Confirm receipt with the recipient and close the record after collection. For medicines, valuables or identity documents, follow the carrier's security rules rather than an informal handover.

articles.title: Reporting an obstructed pedestrian refuge or crossing island
articles.summary: Offline planning and recordkeeping guidance for reporting an obstructed pedestrian refuge or crossing island.

visual.alt: A three-part checklist schematic labelled Location, Access impact, Report. It summarises safe information gathering and planning for reporting an obstructed pedestrian refuge or crossing island, not actual live conditions or a hazardous procedure.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid; current instructions from the responsible organisation take precedence.

sections.title: Understand the local arrangement
paragraphs: A refuge can become difficult to use when debris, equipment or parked objects narrow its space. Describe the location using a road name and nearby junction without entering traffic to inspect it.
Note whether the obstruction appears to affect wheelchair users, pushchairs or anyone needing the island to pause. Never assume an alternative gap in traffic is a safe crossing.

sections.title: Prepare and verify a practical alternative
paragraphs: Use the relevant highway authority's published reporting channel when available. Include a factual description, date and photo only if taken from a safe public position.
Retain a report reference and check for an official response. For immediate danger, use the appropriate local emergency reporting channel; this guide cannot assess live road conditions.

articles.title: Checking access changes on a canal or riverside towpath
articles.summary: Offline planning and recordkeeping guidance for checking access changes on a canal or riverside towpath.

visual.alt: A three-part route schematic labelled Access point, Closure check, Street option. It summarises safe information gathering and planning for checking access changes on a canal or riverside towpath, not actual live conditions or a hazardous procedure.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid; current instructions from the responsible organisation take precedence.

sections.title: Understand the local arrangement
paragraphs: Towpaths and riverside paths may have different managers, gates, steps and restricted sections. Record the named waterway, nearest public access point and responsible organisation where known.
A closure notice may apply only to a short section. An old downloaded map does not prove a route remains passable, especially after severe weather or flooding.

sections.title: Prepare and verify a practical alternative
paragraphs: Before a non-essential journey, identify a public street or accessible path alternative that does not require approaching floodwater or entering a closed area. Consider lighting, surfaces and step-free access.
Keep a dated note of the source consulted. Follow current signage and the responsible organisation's instructions; do not move barriers or take an unverified shortcut along the water.

articles.title: Planning around unavailable mobility-aid parking at public venues
articles.summary: Offline planning and recordkeeping guidance for planning around unavailable mobility-aid parking at public venues.

visual.alt: A three-part checklist schematic labelled Ask venue, Confirm space, Review. It summarises safe information gathering and planning for planning around unavailable mobility-aid parking at public venues, not actual live conditions or a hazardous procedure.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid; current instructions from the responsible organisation take precedence.

sections.title: Understand the local arrangement
paragraphs: A venue may change where scooters, wheelchairs or other aids can be positioned during works. Ask staff about accessible entry, available space and whether an aid can remain with its user.
Do not assume informal storage is authorised or secure. Never obstruct exits, corridors or accessible routes, or leave an aid somewhere that prevents its user from leaving independently.

sections.title: Prepare and verify a practical alternative
paragraphs: Record the venue's confirmed arrangement, who provided it and any limitations affecting the visit. Include a way to contact staff if the agreed space becomes unavailable.
Review the plan before each visit while temporary changes remain. If essential accessibility needs cannot be met, ask about reasonable alternatives instead of improvising an unsafe arrangement.

articles.title: Verifying contact details printed on temporary public notices
articles.summary: Offline planning and recordkeeping guidance for verifying contact details printed on temporary public notices.

visual.alt: A three-part sequence schematic labelled Notice, Independent check, Record. It summarises safe information gathering and planning for verifying contact details printed on temporary public notices, not actual live conditions or a hazardous procedure.
visual.caption: Offline planning aid; current instructions from the responsible organisation take precedence.

sections.title: Understand the local arrangement
paragraphs: A printed notice can be useful without internet, but a phone number or QR code on it does not prove authenticity. Record the named organisation, affected service and date without assuming the notice is current.

Compare contact details with an independently established number from a trusted household record or the responsible organisation. Never share passwords or payment details merely because a notice requests them.

sections.title: Prepare and verify a practical alternative
paragraphs: If confirmed, record the notice date, affected service and the independent confirmation source. Clearly distinguish verified contacts from unverified numbers printed on the notice.
When notices conflict, seek clarification through an established organisational channel. This is a verification aid, not a statement about any live incident or service status.
